Well that's not going to be the only issue as the quality has suddenly plummeted. We have had two pair rip now! Both in the size J3. Before this we only had to buy more when he grew out of them. He has been wearing this style of croc rainboots for 5 years and suddenly went through two pair in under a year! Maybe things didn't change. Maybe they only go up to J3 because the larger size creates issues in the quality, but if that's they case they shouldn't go beyond J2. We love these boots and I have no clue what I'm going to do now that they're basically garbage! The pink ones are under 3 months old and just started ripping. negative_reviews.title: Avoid If You Have A Wide Foot
negative_reviews.text: First of all, you need to avoid these (and all Reefs for that matter) if you do not have a narrow foot. Even those with a slightly wide foot will feel like they are cramped and falling off the sides of this flip flop. Most flip flops fit my W/2E foot perfectly fine, but these are not even close to a comfortable fit. The main issue is the narrow foot bed. The secondary issue is the tight strap (though that will relax a bit after use). I have found these issues across Reef's entire line. Some people will recommend going a 1/2 or full size up to accommodate, but that just doesn't help. I am a 10.5, ordered an 11, and it's still tight. Went to a local store to try on a 12 and it was longer but still tight and narrow. The longer size did offer a little more width in the foot bed, but my foot was still close to hanging off the sides and didn't feel stable. Just compare a Reef to another flip flop and see how much smaller the foot bed can be. When you wear a flip flop, you don't want your foot to fill the foot bed, side to side. You want some room there. That never happens with Reefs. You will catch yourself looking at the tag to make sure you didn't get a pair of woman's flip flops. That's how narrow Reefs run. Second, if you don't have high arches, avoid this sandal. The arch support is nice, but it is high, so those with low arches will just feel pressure all day long. I have normal to slightly high arches and even I feel the pressure from the arch support. Lastly, as a couple other reviews mentioned, these are basically glorified pool/beach flip flops. They are built more for purpose than comfort, with a rubbery foot bed and gripping sole. I doubt these are the pair you'd choose to wear to go walking around town in the summer months. For about $20, you probably shouldn't expect much more than that anyway (though, admittedly, I kind of did). With all that said, Reef does make a good product that lasts. But, sadly, they have a very narrow market for their products, literally and figuratively.

However, yesterday in the rain I quickly learned the truth about these boots. As my son sat digging in the mud at the park (wearing rain pants pulled OVER the ankles of the boots mind you) it seems the water was actually being absorbed by the boot like a sponge... negative_reviews.title: No gel in pads. Threads ripped immediately.
negative_reviews.text: When I first tried one of the gloves on & then clasped the wrist velcro pull closure to remove it, the threads ripped around the entire circumference of the velcro pull tab. Being a seamstress, I tested the strength of one of the segments of thread by attempting to break it with my fingers. Sure enough, it broke in half with little effort. I’m nearly certain the thread is cotton, which easily decomposes if left damp in high humidity. Thin cotton thread is not strong enough or appropriate for cycling/sport gloves. Secondly, I immediately sensed there was no gel in the palms because the padding squished like thin foam. Upon examining the inside of the gloves, I validated I was correct. Every stitched area that was advertised to have "gel pads" instead had thin foam protruding 2 to 3 mm beyond the stitching. In other words, simple foam, like the kind you would see on wire hangars coming from your local dry cleaners, was sewn into the interior of the gloves - NOT gel. My previous cycle gloves had real gel pads, & the difference was profound. Those gloves had not been expensive either, so there’s no excuse for this rip-off. I have no problem with not having brand name, well-made, fancy gloves. (For example, I would've been willing to hot glue thesse velcro wrist tabs back together.) However, I have a big issue with false advertisement.

negative_reviews.text: UPDATE: Got a hole in the palm of one glove after about 10 months. Gloves are still "usable" although not really desirable at this point. My original review is still spot-on. ORIGINAL REVIEW: I cycle daily and own many, many cycling gloves. I generally get 1 or 2 years out of each pair. I ordered these because my (old) half-finger road gloves finally started coming apart. I had read very good reviews of this glove both on multiple listings here on Amazon as well as another popular import e-commerce site. Honestly, these gloves look like they have the worst quality of ANY cycling gloves I've ever purchased. I concede that the jury is still out on how long they'll last, but the padding is utter garbage and the stitching is lacking. I've got absolutely nothing against inexpensive cycling gear from China (like these gloves). I've still got multiple pairs of GREAT Chinese cycling gloves I purchased from Amazon. They could easily have put better cushioning on the palm (what's in there sure isn't gel like they claim). The only people who should buy these gloves are folks who ride maybe 2 or 3 short rides a year. Anybody who actually cycles daily/weekly/monthly needs to look elsewhere.

The single glove, representative of the pair, was not very well padded at all; it felt like it had rubber grips sewn directly to the palm fabric with zero cushioning inside. I bought these gloves to use as protection against self-harm by an autistic individual, and even if there had been two, they would have been useless for this purpose. I am returning the glove and looking for a different brand, possibly from a different website.

(Yes, both shoes were tied) Luckily I fell the right direction-- few feet more sideways would have been a rapid tumble down the side of the red rocks. WHY have SPEED HOOKs on the side of "hiking" boots? And why have the lacing holes on the boots so small that the laces won't go through without the tips (aglets), so that you need speed hooks? negative_reviews.title: I really wanted to like these ...
negative_reviews.text: I really wanted to like these, but they simply have too many basic flaws. To their credit, they are incredibly light and they look nice. Unfortunately, that is about the extent of what they have to offer. While they use the same last as the Vasque Snowblime and fit as expected in terms of length and width, they are a lower volume shoe. Even with a light hiking sock or running sock, they are a little snug on top of the boot when fully loosened. As these are made of synthetic fabric rather than leather, it's unlikely there will be much, if any, expansion after breaking them in. The primary issue, however, is that they leaked before I even left the house with them. About 10 minutes after I first put them on, I went to the sink to fill the dogs' water bowl. As I was doing so, I splashed some water on the lower half of the tongue of the boot. The water immediately soaked through. These are supposed to be a waterproof SNOW boot, designed to keep your feet dry for hours of hiking in the snow and slush - and yet they leaked in my kitchen. After that, there was really nothing I could do with these. I opted instead to keep the Vasque Snowblimes, which I purchased alongside these. Although those also leak, they are a higher volume shoe that can accommodate a heavier sock and hopefully, will be able to withstand the snow after I soak them down in silicone waterproofing spray.

I loved my soon to be three year old Teva Deckers (first Tevas I have owned) so much I looked for a new pair. Unfortunately, Teva in what now appears to be their incompetent managements wisdom - has chosen not to make them anymore - so I compromised for the Mush II. Huge mistake and disappointment. My problems with the Mush Ii are the following: 1. Though my Deckers and the Mush II are size 10 - the Mush II is more than 3/4 of an inch shorter and 3/8" narrower than the Deckers - which fit perfectly. The Mush II is too small. They fit my wife. 2. In the Amazon photos the Mush II - Dune model has what appears to a shade of olive green faded straps which I was fine with. In reality the straps are faded tan or beige - and but ugly. 3. Not only are the straps faded and ugly, but they are made of cotton which will not last if I wear these in wet environments - cotton rots quickly when wet frequently. The Mush (aptly descriptive term) apparently made by some incompetent factory with no supervision of quality control by Teva. Very disappointed. My wife told me she would give me $ 5.00 for them and sew some embroidered ribbon over the straps so they aren't so but ugly - I should have taken it. Mush II is no better than the $7.00 flops I also have, surely won't last any longer (turns out in the 18 months I have had them I have had to re-glue the soles twice and the straps have come out once. Really, don't waste you money on this Mush. Carefully checkout what ever you consider buying from Teva - because they are not managing quality control as evinced by the Mush. My conclusion is that I either got lucky with my Teva Deckers - or Teva has lost all quality control and design abilities, management competence and their current business model is ripoff of their loyal customers.

negative_reviews.title: These shoes aren't made for walking
negative_reviews.text: I wanted to love these shoes so badly. They're beautifully made, with classic styling and an admirable attention to detail. There's a decent amount of cushioning in the insole, which boded well. Loved the black, scaled look, the stacked heeled, the little silver tips on the ties, and they slipped right on my feet as if they were made for them...until I took a few steps. Then, ouch! I have never tried to walk in anything so painful. The leather is stiff and hard on the sides and comes up high in the back, where it rubbed against and immediately -- I'm talking in under 10 steps-- left a painful red mark on my Achilles that had me limping. I could not get out of these shoes fast enough. My left foot still smarts, but the size appeared to be right. It's just the cut of the shoe itself and the hardness of the leather than seemed to cause the issue. Although I suspect these shoes look nice and must work for someone, I couldn't recommend them to anyone who values comfort.

negative_reviews.title: Slim toe-box, Stiff to break in

The toe-box is tight with very little wriggle room for your toes. The rest of the shoe is also slim, and it has very little arch support. While the design is nice, the heel have little traction and the leather is stiff. That stiffness alone makes it hard to break in this pair to wear them long term...especially the back heel area. (Don't be surprised if you end up getting a bit of painful marks as the shoes rub against your skin. Ouch.) The loafer looks great, if it was just on the shelf. But in real daily use, I felt like I was simply wearing a plank of slippery wood-piece under my feet.

negative_reviews.text: When I got these in the mail I noticed that the shoe was constructed of a really thin material. I worried how well they would hold up (how long they would last). But they did feel comfortable enough on, while walking around the house. I went online and read so many reviews about the sole of this model being made of cheap foam instead of rubber, which has caused them to wear out on the bottoms really quickly (about 4 to 6 weeks for other reviewers). Rather than take a chance, I decided to return mine. The "Sketchers Sport" were a stronger build, but more like a running shoe. You could tell a real difference in construct, between the two. Normally I wear Nikes because they have the extra padding insole and harder, rubber sole that can withstand years of heavy walking. I need to have cushioning inside my sneakers. These didn't have that. The Sketchers did look really nice in grey & blue combo, but I could tell from the construct, that they would not last very long. If the price had been lower I may have kept them and planned on buying another pair in a few months. But I thought $50 to $60 was too much to spend for a shoe that would wear out quickly.

negative_reviews.title: They wear fast, it's true... But...
negative_reviews.text: (I want to be clear - I loved this shoe. The one-star is only due to a recent manufacturing decision from Sketchers) These were a game-changer for me at work. Years and years on my feet, lifting, twisting, and walking had taken a toll on my knees, heels, arches etc. As long as I kept moving I was fine, but stop - even for a few moments - and I was stiff and sore. The car ride home left me hobbling to the front door and in the morning I was nearly crippled by pain and stiffness - coupled with restless sleep from throbbing pain in my feet and legs. I am good at what I do and well-compensated due to my longevity with my employer, at this stage of my life starting over is just not an option, so finding another job - as some suggest - is right out. Do I spend the rest of my life and career like an invalid? I hope not to. So, after much trial and error (as well as money wasted and a closet full of barely-worn sneakers) hoping to find a shoe that made a difference, I had found it in the Go Walk. As I said, it was a game-changer. Pain? Gone. Stiffness? Gone. Was I replacing them every 4-5 months over the last two years? Yes. Did I care? Nope. Lightweight, flexible, cushioned, supportive *exactly* where I needed it (the sole) and not where I didn't (everywhere else, because it restricts my movement) - Take my money, Sketchers. My final downfall? This shoe is no longer being made in the 'E' width - my feet are short, but wide along with a high instep; I will not "go up a size" to accommodate width because that results in a ridiculously long toe I end up tripping over. I know it's just a shoe - but I am saddened by this decision from Sketchers. I will try something similar, but the exact combination of design in *this* shoe is what worked so well for me, and I am not hopeful. I did send comment to Sketchers directly - not that I expect them to cater to me exclusively - but maybe if others have the same issue I do, and also make their opinions known it would be financially beneficial for Sketchers to reconsider.

I noticed that when I wore them, I had significant heel pain at the end of the day that I didn't' have when wearing other shoes. I don't think they have enough heel support, the heel is low and the sole is very flexible and doesn't provide good support. I'm tossing. Sorry, Skechers, I have bought over a dozen pairs of your shoes and these are the first ones that disappointed me.

negative_reviews.title: Poorly constructed :(
negative_reviews.text: I bought these shoes in early August, it's now November and the bottom right shoe has decent size hole in it. The other shoe is close to looking the same way. negative_reviews.title: Not very comfortable

description: THE STORY OF BEARPAW In 2001, a young Tom Romeo was searching for a sign that would help him choose between his two passions. Like many people, Tom has a special spot that is his “happy place”, where he finds time to meditate and listen to nature. While sitting on the special rock located on the shores of Lake Tahoe, a massive bear suddenly paused a short ways away from him, stared directly at him for a moment, and decided to move along without any confrontation. This magical experience had to be some sort of sign, and it inspired Tom to seek out the meaning of this encounter. Tom soon learned that a bear crossing is viewed by many as a sign of good luck and while symbolizing strength, the bear serves as a guide for many at an impasse. All doubt had gone away for Tom and he knew this was an opportunity to start his own shoe company founded on this great animal, with the name BEARPAW as an homage to his chance meeting with that bear in Tahoe. Shortly after, the very first BEARPAW boot style was created, called EVA. Since then, the EVA has evolved into our ELLE boot, and is still the most popular shoe style in the company’s collection. Both EVA and ELLE embodied the BEARPAW lifestyle with their warmth and effortless style. The BEARPAW team now creates shoe styles for all walks of life, so you can live life comfortably wherever you are.

negative_reviews.title: Very confusing
negative_reviews.text: I unboxed these shoes in my bedroom, which has a polyester carpet (important). I put the shoes on (they fit well) while sitting down, stood up.... and had to grab a chair to prevent myself from slipping over. I felt as though I was standing on wet ice! I carefully walked downstairs to the living room, sat down, and removed the shoes so that I could see what kind of strange super-slippery material the soles were made out of. (Picture 1.) I saw that there was a sticker on each sole, although oddly it felt less slippery than the rest of the sole. And on closer inspection (picture 2) it was clear that the sole was simply a thin layer of slippery plastic, which was already peeling away at the seams. Unacceptable. UPDATE: OK, I decided to see what would happen if I peeled off the thin plastic layer, and after wrestling with it for several minutes (it didn't come off easily), underneath there were perfectly functional rubber-like soles. It would have been nice if there had been some instructions - I certainly haven't seen this before. Since the danger of slipping over had been eliminated, I tried walking around in them. The fit is OK (I'd got one size up to accommodate my wide feet). However, the arch is uncomfortable: it's too far back, so that the highest point is under the front of my heel rather than underneath the instep.
